Image Compressor Online

A general-purpose image compressor with presets from 20KB to 500KB and a custom size option.

Compression tool

Target size Target size:
Advanced settings

By default the tool keeps quality reasonable (about 62% or higher) and reduces dimensions to reach small targets; tick “Keep dimensions” to prefer full size at lower quality. Aspect ratio is always preserved and images are never enlarged. PNG is lossless and may not reach a small target; JPEG/WebP are lossy. JPEG replaces transparency with white; WebP and PNG keep it.

Choose your target

Use the presets or type a custom size. For specific sizes see the 20KB, 50KB, 100KB, 200KB and 500KB tools.

JPEG, WebP or PNG?

JPEG and WebP are lossy and can reach small sizes. PNG is lossless and best for graphics and transparency.

One tool, many target sizes

This is the general-purpose page. Use the presets for 20KB, 50KB, 100KB, 200KB or 500KB, or type any value from 1 to 10,240 KB. The tool reports whether the target was reached, along with real sizes and dimensions.

For common sizes, dedicated pages explain the practical details: compress image to 20KB, 100KB, 200KB and more.

Squoosh image compression and this tool

Many people searching for "squoosh image compression" are looking for a free browser-based way to shrink pictures. Squoosh is an open-source image compression app from Google Chrome Labs. It runs in the browser, lets you compare codecs side by side, and gives manual control over settings such as quality.

ImageTo20KB approaches the problem differently. Instead of asking you to tune sliders until the file looks right, you tell it the file size you need and it searches for the best fit. That suits forms and portals with a hard KB limit. If you want to fine-tune codecs and compare formats manually, a tool like Squoosh is a good choice; we are not affiliated with it. If you need an exact KB target quickly, use the presets here.

How the tool decides

For JPEG and WebP it tries quality levels, measures the real size each time and keeps the highest quality that fits. If needed it reduces dimensions gradually. For PNG it encodes once, because PNG is lossless.

Limits to know

Files above 50 MB or 50 megapixels are rejected. Animated GIF, animated WebP, SVG and HEIC are not supported. Results depend on your browser, your image and the target. Always keep the original.

Which page should I use?

Use this page when you want to choose the size yourself. Use the 20KB page for very strict limits, the 100KB or 200KB pages for typical uploads, and the 500KB page for higher quality. The online forms page explains how to prepare photos and signatures for portals, and the resizer is for setting maximum pixel dimensions.

Formats explained

JPEG suits photographs and is the most widely accepted. WebP is often smaller and supports transparency but is not accepted by every form. PNG is lossless and best for graphics. The format list shows only what your browser can really encode, so a missing option is a browser limitation.

Good habits for any compression job

Always keep the original. Compress once, from the best source you have. Set a target based on a real requirement, not a guess. Check the preview at full size. Prefer reducing dimensions over pushing quality extremely low. And remember that a smaller file is not always a better one, because a picture that is too small or too blurry may fail the purpose it was meant for. Use the related pages below for the target you need.

Unsupported files

Animated GIFs and animated WebP files are rejected so that animation is never silently removed. SVG files are vector graphics and are rejected rather than rendered. HEIC photos from some phones should first be exported as JPG on the device.

Common questions

Is there a limit on image size?

Files over 50 MB or 50 megapixels are rejected to protect your browser from running out of memory.
